lessons.solution:
steps = ["read prices", "reject negatives", "add prices", "apply discount", "show total"]
print(" -> ".join(steps))

en.objectives: Write five steps for calculating a shopping total, including validation.
en.body:
An algorithm is a finite set of steps that transforms an input into a result. Write the steps before choosing a programming language. A recipe with an unspecified quantity or no stopping point is ambiguous; a program needs precise operations and an outcome you can check.

enumerate starts numbering at one without changing the list. Each printed row is one operation; the ordering is part of the algorithm, so validating after displaying a result would change its meaning.

Practice: Write five steps for calculating a shopping total, including validation.

Checkpoint: Rejecting a negative price belongs before adding it to a shopping total.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: enumerate starts numbering at one without changing the list. Each printed row is one operation; the ordering is part of the algorithm, so validating after displaying a result would change its meaning.
en.mistake: Do not confuse an informal goal with executable steps.
en.hint: enumerate starts numbering at one without changing the list. Each printed row is one operation; the ordering is part of the algorithm, so validating after displaying a result would change its meaning.
en.challenge: Write five steps for calculating a shopping total, including validation.
en.question: Which property makes an algorithm usable?
en.explanation: enumerate starts numbering at one without changing the list. Each printed row is one operation; the ordering is part of the algorithm, so validating after displaying a result would change its meaning.

my.objectives: ဈေးဝယ်စုစုပေါင်း တွက်ရန် input စစ်ခြင်းပါသော အဆင့်ငါးဆင့် ရေးပါ။
my.body:
Algorithm သည် input မှ ရလဒ်တစ်ခု ရရှိရန် တိကျသော အဆင့်များကို အစဉ်လိုက် လုပ်ဆောင်ခြင်းဖြစ်သည်။ Language မရွေးမီ လိုအပ်သည့် input၊ ဆောင်ရွက်ပုံနှင့် ရပ်တန့်မည့်နေရာကို စာဖြင့် အရင်ရေးပါ။

enumerate သည် စာရင်းကို မပြောင်းဘဲ တစ်မှစ၍ နံပါတ်တပ်သည်။ စစ်ဆေးပြီးမှ တွက်ချက်ရသဖြင့် အဆင့်အစဉ်လည်း အရေးကြီးသည်။ ရလဒ်ပြပြီးမှ input စစ်ခြင်းက လုပ်ငန်း၏ အဓိပ္ပာယ်ကို ပြောင်းစေသည်။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — ဈေးဝယ်စုစုပေါင်း တွက်ရန် input စစ်ခြင်းပါသော အဆင့်ငါးဆင့် ရေးပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — ဈေးနှုန်း negative ကို total ထဲ မပေါင်းမီ ပယ်မည်ဟု flow ရေးပါ။

နမူနာကို မပြင်မီ ထွက်မည့်အဖြေနှင့် ကိုယ်စစ်လိုသည့် ယူဆချက်ကို စာဖြင့် ကြိုမှတ်ပါ။ Input တစ်ခုစီသာ ပြောင်းစမ်းပြီး တကယ့်ရလဒ်နှင့် ခန့်မှန်းချက်ကို နှိုင်းယှဉ်ပါ။ မတူသည့်နေရာကို အကြောင်းရင်း ရှင်းရေးပြီး မူရင်းနမူနာကို ပြန်ကြည့်နိုင်အောင် ထိန်းထားပါ။ Input တစ်မျိုးတွင် မှန်ရုံဖြင့် အခြေအနေအားလုံး မှန်ကြောင်း မယူဆပါနှင့်။

title.my: Input၊ Processing နှင့် Output

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
minutes = 12
seconds = minutes * 60
print(f"{seconds} seconds")
lessons.solution:
minutes = 7
seconds = minutes * 60
print(seconds, "seconds")

en.objectives: Convert 7 minutes to seconds and label the result.
en.body:
Keep the source data, the transformation and the presentation separate. This makes it easier to test the calculation without a keyboard or screen. A unit is part of the meaning of a value: twelve minutes and twelve seconds are different inputs even though both contain the number twelve.

The variable minutes is the input, multiplication is the transformation, and print is the output. For seven minutes the expected result is 420 seconds; checking that value catches a mistaken division.

Practice: Convert 7 minutes to seconds and label the result.

Checkpoint: Write minutes and seconds beside the intermediate values in your trace.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The variable minutes is the input, multiplication is the transformation, and print is the output. For seven minutes the expected result is 420 seconds; checking that value catches a mistaken division.
en.mistake: Always carry the unit through the calculation.
en.hint: The variable minutes is the input, multiplication is the transformation, and print is the output. For seven minutes the expected result is 420 seconds; checking that value catches a mistaken division.
en.challenge: Convert 7 minutes to seconds and label the result.
en.question: What is the processing step?
en.explanation: The variable minutes is the input, multiplication is the transformation, and print is the output. For seven minutes the expected result is 420 seconds; checking that value catches a mistaken division.

title.my: Program ကို တစ်ဆင့်ချင်း လိုက်ကြည့်ခြင်း

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
balance = 10
balance = balance + 5
balance = balance - 3
print(balance)
lessons.solution:
balance = 20
balance += 8
balance -= 6
print(balance)

en.objectives: Trace a balance of 20, add 8, subtract 6 and predict output.
en.body:
A trace records the state after each statement. Make a table with a line number and the current variable values rather than guessing the final output. Assignment replaces a binding; it is not a mathematical equation that must remain true forever.

The successive states are 10, 15 and 12. The last print reads the current binding 12; it does not remember the original value unless you store that value separately.

Practice: Trace a balance of 20, add 8, subtract 6 and predict output.

Checkpoint: Keep a separate row for each assignment rather than overwriting the trace.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The successive states are 10, 15 and 12. The last print reads the current binding 12; it does not remember the original value unless you store that value separately.
en.mistake: Trace the right-hand expression before updating the left-hand variable.
en.hint: The successive states are 10, 15 and 12. The last print reads the current binding 12; it does not remember the original value unless you store that value separately.
en.challenge: Trace a balance of 20, add 8, subtract 6 and predict output.
en.question: What is the final balance in the example?
en.explanation: The successive states are 10, 15 and 12. The last print reads the current binding 12; it does not remember the original value unless you store that value separately.

en.objectives: Print a truth table for is_member or has_pass.
en.body:
Boolean expressions describe decisions using True and False. The operator and requires both conditions, or permits either, and not reverses a condition. Construct all combinations to check a rule; one successful example is not enough to establish that access logic is correct.

Two nested loops enumerate four combinations. Only the True, True row satisfies and, so the table exposes a mistaken or condition that would admit three combinations instead of one.

Practice: Print a truth table for is_member or has_pass.

Checkpoint: Test the both-false row as well as the both-true row.

my.objectives: is_member or has_pass အတွက် အမှန်တန်ဖိုးဇယား ပြပါ။
my.body:
Boolean logic တွင် True/False ဖြင့် ဆုံးဖြတ်သည်။ and သည် နှစ်ခုလုံး မှန်ရန်လိုပြီး or သည် အနည်းဆုံးတစ်ခု မှန်လျှင် ရသည်။ စည်းမျဉ်းမှန်မမှန် သိရန် ဖြစ်နိုင်သမျှ အတွဲအားလုံးကို စစ်ပါ။

Loop နှစ်ထပ်က ဖြစ်နိုင်သော အတွဲလေးခုကို ပြသည်။ True နှစ်ခုပါသော အတန်းတစ်ခုသာ and ကို ဖြည့်ဆည်းသည်။ or ဟု မှားရေးမိပါက သုံးအတန်း မှန်သွားမည်ကို ဇယားက ပြသည်။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — is_member or has_pass အတွက် အမှန်တန်ဖိုးဇယား ပြပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — နှစ်ခုလုံးမှားသောအတွဲနှင့် နှစ်ခုလုံးမှန်သောအတွဲကိုပါ စစ်ပါ။

နမူနာကို မပြင်မီ ထွက်မည့်အဖြေနှင့် ကိုယ်စစ်လိုသည့် ယူဆချက်ကို စာဖြင့် ကြိုမှတ်ပါ။ Input တစ်ခုစီသာ ပြောင်းစမ်းပြီး တကယ့်ရလဒ်နှင့် ခန့်မှန်းချက်ကို နှိုင်းယှဉ်ပါ။ မတူသည့်နေရာကို အကြောင်းရင်း ရှင်းရေးပြီး မူရင်းနမူနာကို ပြန်ကြည့်နိုင်အောင် ထိန်းထားပါ။ Input တစ်မျိုးတွင် မှန်ရုံဖြင့် အခြေအနေအားလုံး မှန်ကြောင်း မယူဆပါနှင့်။

en.objectives: Create area(width, height) and a separate message function.
en.body:
Decomposition breaks a large task into pieces with clear responsibilities. A calculation function can return a number while a presentation function builds a message. Give each function an explicit input and output so it can be reused and tested without unrelated side effects.

sum calculates 10 and receipt formats that value. Keeping formatting outside subtotal lets the same total be shown in a terminal, saved to a file or tested with an assertion.

Practice: Create area(width, height) and a separate message function.

Checkpoint: A total-calculation function should not require a screen to be tested.

en.objectives: Count total and unique course registrations from a list.
en.body:
Choose a collection based on the question you need to answer. Lists preserve sequence and duplicates; sets represent unique membership. Converting a list to a set loses repetition information. Sort a set before producing a predictable presentation rather than relying on its iteration order.

There are three visits but two unique names. sorted returns a new list for display; it does not turn the set into an ordered data model or restore the duplicate visit.

Practice: Count total and unique course registrations from a list.

Checkpoint: Keep the original visits when you also need to count repeated visitors.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: There are three visits but two unique names. sorted returns a new list for display; it does not turn the set into an ordered data model or restore the duplicate visit.
en.mistake: Do not use a set when repeated events matter.

lessons.code:

price = Decimal("0.10")

en.objectives: Calculate three items priced 0.25 using Decimal strings.
en.body:
A data type defines both representation and available operations. Use integer counts, Boolean flags and text identifiers deliberately. Decimal arithmetic is useful when decimal precision is part of the requirement; construct Decimal from text to avoid importing a binary float approximation.

The string "0.10" expresses a decimal value directly. Starting with 0.1 as a float can carry its existing approximation into Decimal; converting types does not repair information that was already lost.

Practice: Calculate three items priced 0.25 using Decimal strings.

Checkpoint: An account code such as 0012 is often an identifier rather than a quantity.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The string "0.10" expresses a decimal value directly. Starting with 0.1 as a float can carry its existing approximation into Decimal; converting types does not repair information that was already lost.
en.mistake: Never assume every identifier should be numeric; leading zeroes can matter.
en.hint: The string "0.10" expresses a decimal value directly. Starting with 0.1 as a float can carry its existing approximation into Decimal; converting types does not repair information that was already lost.

en.objectives: Test your search with first, last and missing values.
en.body:
Linear search checks elements one at a time and stops at the first match. Define a missing-result contract before writing callers. None is distinct from index zero; treating a zero index as false can incorrectly report that the first element was not found.

The example returns 1 because the match is the second element. The first element would return 0, while an absent value returns None; callers must compare with None explicitly.

Practice: Test your search with first, last and missing values.

Checkpoint: An empty list is an additional search case: it should return the missing result.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The example returns 1 because the match is the second element. The first element would return 0, while an absent value returns None; callers must compare with None explicitly.
en.mistake: Do not put the missing return inside the loop.
en.hint: The example returns 1 because the match is the second element. The first element would return 0, while an absent value returns None; callers must compare with None explicitly.

title.my: Sorting နှင့် မူရင်းကို မပြောင်းခြင်း

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
scores = [7, 2, 9]
ranked = sorted(scores, reverse=True)
print(scores)
print(ranked)
lessons.solution:
names = ["Mandalay", "Mya", "Ko"]
ranked = sorted(names, key=len)
print(names)
print(ranked)

en.objectives: Sort names by length while preserving the original list.
en.body:
Sorting arranges values using a comparison key. sorted creates a new list, while list.sort changes the existing list and returns None. Choose intentionally when callers still need the input order, such as recording when learners submitted their scores.

The original scores stay [7, 2, 9], and ranked becomes [9, 7, 2]. Assigning ranked = scores.sort() would instead bind ranked to None even though scores was successfully reordered.

Practice: Sort names by length while preserving the original list.

Checkpoint: Compare original and ranked after sorting to make mutation visible.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The original scores stay [7, 2, 9], and ranked becomes [9, 7, 2]. Assigning ranked = scores.sort() would instead bind ranked to None even though scores was successfully reordered.
en.mistake: Check whether a collection method mutates or returns a new value.
en.hint: The original scores stay [7, 2, 9], and ranked becomes [9, 7, 2]. Assigning ranked = scores.sort() would instead bind ranked to None even though scores was successfully reordered.
en.challenge: Sort names by length while preserving the original list.
en.question: What does list.sort return?
en.explanation: The original scores stay [7, 2, 9], and ranked becomes [9, 7, 2]. Assigning ranked = scores.sort() would instead bind ranked to None even though scores was successfully reordered.

my.objectives: နာမည်များကို အရှည်အလိုက် စီပြီး မူရင်းစာရင်း မပြောင်းပါနှင့်။
my.body:
Sorting သည် comparison key အလိုက် အစဉ်ချခြင်းဖြစ်သည်။ sorted က list အသစ်ပေးပြီး list.sort က မူရင်း list ကို ပြင်သည်။ ရောက်လာသည့်အစဉ်ကို နောက်မှလိုသေးလျှင် မူရင်းကို ထိန်းသော နည်းရွေးပါ။

scores မူရင်းသည် [7, 2, 9] အတိုင်း ရှိပြီး ranked က [9, 7, 2] ဖြစ်သည်။ ranked = scores.sort() ဟု ရေးပါက မူရင်းကို စီပြီးသော်လည်း ranked သည် None ဖြစ်မည်။

en.objectives: Compare a single loop count with a nested-loop pair count for n = 5.
en.body:
Time complexity describes how work grows as input size grows, rather than the exact seconds on one phone. A single traversal grows linearly; traversing every pair grows quadratically. Count meaningful operations on small examples before using asymptotic notation.

A pair traversal does n times n units of work. Moving from five items to ten increases pairs from 25 to 100, so a small-looking input change can make a quadratic algorithm much more expensive.

Practice: Compare a single loop count with a nested-loop pair count for n = 5.

Checkpoint: Count operations for n=5 and n=10 before comparing elapsed seconds.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: A pair traversal does n times n units of work. Moving from five items to ten increases pairs from 25 to 100, so a small-looking input change can make a quadratic algorithm much more expensive.
en.mistake: Big-O is a growth model, not a promise about wall-clock timing.
en.hint: A pair traversal does n times n units of work. Moving from five items to ten increases pairs from 25 to 100, so a small-looking input change can make a quadratic algorithm much more expensive.

အတွဲတိုင်း ပတ်ပါက n × n ကြိမ် လုပ်ရသည်။ ငါးခုမှ ဆယ်ခု ပြောင်းလျှင် အတွဲ ၂၅ မှ ၁၀၀ ဖြစ်သဖြင့် input အနည်းငယ် တိုးခြင်းပင် အလုပ်များစေနိုင်သည်။

en.objectives: Create a practice file, stage it, and inspect the staged diff.
en.body:
Git records snapshots of a project. The working directory contains current edits; the staging area selects what the next commit will contain. Inspect the staged diff before committing. These commands create a new practice directory and do not change any existing repository.

git add copies the current file content into the staging area. Further edits are not staged automatically; compare both git diff and git diff --cached to understand the two snapshots.

Practice: Create a practice file, stage it, and inspect the staged diff.

Checkpoint: Edit the practice file after staging and compare the two diff views again.

en.body:
A branch is a movable name for a commit, not a second copy of the whole project. Make a small feature branch and review its commits before proposing a merge. Check for local edits before switching; uncommitted work can follow you between branches when the switch is allowed.

git switch -c creates and checks out the branch at the current commit. It needs a valid repository state; commit a first snapshot in the disposable lab before practicing history commands.

Practice: In a committed practice repository, create feature/notes and inspect its history.

Checkpoint: A new feature branch initially points to the same commit as its starting point.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.

title.my: Database Table နှင့် Primary Key

lessons.solution:
INSERT INTO learners (id, name) VALUES (2, 'Ko');
SELECT id, name FROM learners ORDER BY id;

en.objectives: Add learner 2 with a different name, then select both rows.
en.body:
A relational table stores rows with a consistent column structure. A primary key identifies a row even when people share a display name. Use constraints to state requirements in the database rather than depending on every client to remember them. Run this example in a new disposable SQLite database.

PRIMARY KEY prevents two rows from using the same identifier. NOT NULL prevents a missing name; neither constraint proves that a real-world name is correct, so validation still has separate responsibilities.

Practice: Add learner 2 with a different name, then select both rows.

Checkpoint: Try a repeated id in the disposable database and read the constraint error.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: PRIMARY KEY prevents two rows from using the same identifier. NOT NULL prevents a missing name; neither constraint proves that a real-world name is correct, so validation still has separate responsibilities.
en.mistake: Never practice CREATE or INSERT on a production database.

lessons.code:
SELECT id, name
FROM learners
WHERE id >= 2
ORDER BY name, id
LIMIT 10;
lessons.solution: SELECT id, name FROM learners ORDER BY name, id LIMIT 5;

en.objectives: Select at most five learners ordered by name and id.
en.body:
WHERE selects matching rows, ORDER BY defines presentation order, and LIMIT bounds the result count. A table has no guaranteed display order without ORDER BY. Add a unique tie-breaker when names can match so repeated requests have a stable ordering.

The example excludes id 1, sorts by name then id, and returns at most ten rows. LIMIT alone does not select the ten most recent learners; that would need a defined timestamp order.

Practice: Select at most five learners ordered by name and id.

Checkpoint: Rows with the same name need id as the tie-breaker in the ordering.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The example excludes id 1, sorts by name then id, and returns at most ten rows. LIMIT alone does not select the ten most recent learners; that would need a defined timestamp order.
en.mistake: Filtering rows is different from sorting them.
en.hint: The example excludes id 1, sorts by name then id, and returns at most ten rows. LIMIT alone does not select the ten most recent learners; that would need a defined timestamp order.

lessons.code:
GET /lessons HTTP/1.1
Host: academy.example
Accept: application/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"count": 120}
lessons.solution:
Method: GET
Path: /lessons
Status: 200
Content-Type: application/json

en.objectives: Identify the method, path, status and content type in the transcript.
en.body:
HTTP connects a request to a response. The method expresses an action, the path identifies a resource, headers describe metadata, and the body carries optional content. This is an illustrative message transcript, not a command to paste into Python or a promise that the example host exists.

The status belongs to the response, while GET belongs to the request. A 200 status says the HTTP operation succeeded; a client must still validate the JSON shape before reading count.

Practice: Identify the method, path, status and content type in the transcript.

Checkpoint: A valid 200 response can still carry a body your client does not understand.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The status belongs to the response, while GET belongs to the request. A 200 status says the HTTP operation succeeded; a client must still validate the JSON shape before reading count.
en.mistake: Do not infer application data from the status number.
en.hint: The status belongs to the response, while GET belongs to the request. A 200 status says the HTTP operation succeeded; a client must still validate the JSON shape before reading count.

en.question: What does status 200 indicate here?
en.explanation: The status belongs to the response, while GET belongs to the request. A 200 status says the HTTP operation succeeded; a client must still validate the JSON shape before reading count.

my.objectives: Transcript မှ method၊ path၊ status နှင့် content type ကို ခွဲရေးပါ။

en.objectives: Reject minutes unless it is an integer between 1 and 180.
en.body:
JSON transports strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects and null. Parsing establishes syntax, not trust or a complete application schema. Check that required fields exist and have the expected type and range before using them. An API contract should state both successful and invalid-input behavior.

A valid JSON value could be null or an array instead of the required object. In Python bool is a subclass of int; use type(value) is int when the contract must reject Boolean values as numbers.

Practice: Reject minutes unless it is an integer between 1 and 180.

Checkpoint: Try a missing minutes key, a string value and a Boolean separately.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.

en.objectives: Test a clamp-to-zero function with negative, zero and positive inputs.
en.body:
A useful test checks observable behavior with independently chosen expected results. Include ordinary data, boundaries and invalid inputs relevant to the contract. A test that repeats the implementation formula can reproduce the same mistake and give false confidence.

The three assertions cover positive, zero and negative input. Assertions are appropriate in teaching tests, but production input validation must not rely on assert because optimized Python can disable it.

Practice: Test a clamp-to-zero function with negative, zero and positive inputs.

Checkpoint: Choose expected values by hand so the test does not copy the same bug.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The three assertions cover positive, zero and negative input. Assertions are appropriate in teaching tests, but production input validation must not rely on assert because optimized Python can disable it.

en.objectives: Call average([]), catch ValueError, and print a useful message.
en.body:
Debugging starts with a reproducible difference between expected and actual behavior. Reduce the input until only the failing condition remains, record the error, form one hypothesis and change one thing. Empty collections often reveal assumptions hidden by normal examples.

The guard stops division by zero and explains the missing requirement. Catching every exception and returning zero would hide the bug and confuse an empty dataset with a real average of zero.

Practice: Call average([]), catch ValueError, and print a useful message.

Checkpoint: Reduce the failing average input to an empty list before proposing a fix.

Before changing the example, predict its result and write down the assumption you are testing. Change one input at a time, compare the actual result with your prediction, and keep a short note explaining any difference. A correct result for one input does not establish every case.
en.lines: The guard stops division by zero and explains the missing requirement. Catching every exception and returning zero would hide the bug and confuse an empty dataset with a real average of zero.
en.mistake: Do not hide unexpected exceptions with a blanket success result.
en.hint: The guard stops division by zero and explains the missing requirement. Catching every exception and returning zero would hide the bug and confuse an empty dataset with a real average of zero.

my.body:

Guard က zero ဖြင့်စားခြင်းကို တားပြီး လိုအပ်ချက်ရှင်းပြသည်။ Exception အားလုံးဖမ်းကာ zero ပြန်လျှင် data မရှိခြင်းနှင့် ပျမ်းမျှ zero တကယ်ဖြစ်ခြင်းကို မခွဲနိုင်တော့ပါ။

en.body:
A requirement describes a user need; an acceptance criterion makes the outcome observable. Replace vague statements such as fast or easy with a concrete workflow and result. Track unverified criteria honestly instead of treating the existence of a screen as evidence that its feature works.

The checklist distinguishes completed behavior from unfinished draft restoration. A useful criterion states an action, its expected result and relevant conditions such as offline operation or account scope.

Practice: Write three acceptance criteria for saving and reopening a note.

Checkpoint: A restore criterion should compare exact text after reopening the app.

en.objectives: Add a third task and display the count of completed tasks.
en.body:
Combine data modeling, iteration and presentation in a small study planner. Represent each task with a title and completion flag instead of maintaining unrelated parallel lists. Start with an in-memory version and defined sample data before adding persistent files or a graphical interface.

The two fields travel together when tasks are reordered or removed. A Boolean flag can drive both the displayed marker and the completion count, so the UI does not need a second conflicting source of truth.

Practice: Add a third task and display the count of completed tasks.

Checkpoint: Reordering task records should keep each title paired with its own status.

HTML describes document structure rather than visual position. A document has metadata in head and visible content in body. Declare a character encoding so Myanmar text is interpreted correctly, and set the document language to help assistive technology choose pronunciation.

The title names the browser document while h1 appears in the page. UTF-8 controls text decoding; it does not install a Myanmar font, so the viewer also needs a suitable font from the device.

Practice: Create a Myanmar-language page with a title and a welcome heading.

Checkpoint: Change lang to my when the primary page content is Myanmar.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Write a course outline with one h1 and two h2 sections.
en.body:
Headings give a document an outline. Use h1 for the primary topic and lower levels for nested sections, choosing by meaning rather than text size. Paragraphs group related sentences. A reader using heading navigation should understand the organization without seeing the visual design.

The h3 belongs under Start here because Practice is a subsection. CSS can change its appearance later without changing this meaning. A collection of bold paragraphs does not provide the same semantic outline.

Practice: Write a course outline with one h1 and two h2 sections.

Checkpoint: Read just the headings aloud and check whether the outline makes sense.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Add a link to a section with id notes.
en.body:
An anchor connects meaningful link text to a destination. A fragment beginning with # points to an element id in the same document. Keep ids unique. This example uses only an internal anchor, so it works in the offline viewer without needing an external website or network permission.

The href fragment must match the target id exactly. Descriptive text such as Read notes tells a learner more than Click here, especially when a screen reader lists links without surrounding paragraphs.

Practice: Add a link to a section with id notes.

Checkpoint: A second element must not reuse the same anchor id.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Create a three-step ordered recipe and an unordered ingredient list.
en.body:
Use an ordered list when the sequence matters, and an unordered list for a collection without a required sequence. Each item belongs in li. List semantics communicate both grouping and item count; typing decorative bullets into ordinary paragraphs loses that information.

Read, Try and Review have an intended order, so ol fits. Editor and Notebook are independent tools, so ul fits. Change the content and decide whether the order still carries meaning.

Practice: Create a three-step ordered recipe and an unordered ingredient list.

Checkpoint: Swapping recipe steps changes meaning; swapping tool names usually does not.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: Read, Try and Review have an intended order, so ol fits. Editor and Notebook are independent tools, so ul fits. Change the content and decide whether the order still carries meaning.
en.mistake: Use nested lists for nested items, not extra line breaks.

en.objectives: Draw a labelled circle with SVG and a visible caption.
en.body:
A graphic needs an accessible description when it communicates information. Inline SVG can provide a scalable illustration without a remote image request. Pair a concise accessible name with a visible caption that explains the takeaway rather than merely saying image.

role="img" treats the SVG as an image and aria-label names it. The visible caption also helps sighted readers. If a chart conveys exact values, provide the numbers as text or a table as well.

Practice: Draw a labelled circle with SVG and a visible caption.

Checkpoint: Describe the trend in the caption rather than only naming the chart colour.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: role="img" treats the SVG as an image and aria-label names it. The visible caption also helps sighted readers. If a chart conveys exact values, provide the numbers as text or a table as well.
en.mistake: Do not communicate a result using colour alone.
en.hint: role="img" treats the SVG as an image and aria-label names it. The visible caption also helps sighted readers. If a chart conveys exact values, provide the numbers as text or a table as well.

role="img" က SVG ကို ပုံအဖြစ် သတ်မှတ်ပြီး aria-label က နာမည်ပေးသည်။ Caption သည် မြင်ရသူကိုလည်း ကူညီသည်။ Chart တွင် တိကျသောကိန်း ရှိလျှင် စာသား သို့မဟုတ် table ဖြင့်ပါ ဖော်ပြပါ။

en.objectives: Add a Wednesday row with 30 minutes while retaining headers.
en.body:
Tables express relationships between rows and columns. A caption names the dataset, th identifies headers and scope connects headers to cells. Use tables for data rather than laying out an entire page; CSS layout handles visual positioning more effectively.

The Monday header applies to its row and Minutes applies to its column. This lets assistive technology relate the value 20 to both labels instead of reading an unexplained sequence of cells.

Practice: Add a Wednesday row with 30 minutes while retaining headers.

Checkpoint: Check that every minutes value can be related to both a day and a header.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

lessons.code: <form><label for="name">Your name</label><input id="name" name="name" autocomplete="name"><label for="age">Age</label><input id="age" name="age" type="number" min="1" max="120"><button type="button">Practice only</button></form>
lessons.solution: <label for="mail">Email</label><input id="mail" name="email" type="email"><button type="button">Preview</button>

en.objectives: Create an email field with a matching label and a practice button.
en.body:
A label describes an input and associates with it using for and id. The name attribute identifies a field when data is submitted; id identifies the element in the document. Choose input types that match the data. This offline example does not submit information to any server.

Clicking a correctly associated label focuses its input. A placeholder is temporary guidance and disappears during typing; it does not replace a persistent accessible label.

Practice: Create an email field with a matching label and a practice button.

Checkpoint: Click the label itself to verify its connection to the intended input.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: Clicking a correctly associated label focuses its input. A placeholder is temporary guidance and disappears during typing; it does not replace a persistent accessible label.
en.mistake: Use fictional details when testing forms.
en.hint: Clicking a correctly associated label focuses its input. A placeholder is temporary guidance and disappears during typing; it does not replace a persistent accessible label.

en.objectives: Change the local range to 1–10 and update the message.
en.body:
Browser constraints provide immediate feedback, but a real server must enforce its own validation. Users can change the page or call an API without the form. Required fields and numeric ranges improve the experience; they do not create an authorization or security boundary.

checkValidity evaluates the declared constraints without sending a request. The result describes this input in this page only. The server cannot trust that a client actually ran these checks.

Practice: Change the local range to 1–10 and update the message.

Checkpoint: Try the blank field, the lower boundary and a value above the upper boundary.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Build header, navigation, main and footer for a learning page.
en.body:
Landmarks identify the role of page regions: header introduces content, nav groups major navigation and main holds the primary content. An article should make sense independently. Meaningful structure reduces dependence on visual styling and helps keyboard and screen-reader navigation.

One visible main region gives the page a clear center. Several navigation regions can be distinguished with accessible names; adding landmarks everywhere without purpose can make navigation noisier.

Practice: Build header, navigation, main and footer for a learning page.

Checkpoint: Give multiple navigation landmarks different accessible names.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: One visible main region gives the page a clear center. Several navigation regions can be distinguished with accessible names; adding landmarks everywhere without purpose can make navigation noisier.
en.mistake: A div with a large font does not become a heading or landmark.
en.hint: One visible main region gives the page a clear center. Several navigation regions can be distinguished with accessible names; adding landmarks everywhere without purpose can make navigation noisier.

en.objectives: Add a warning class with a readable text colour and padding.
en.body:
CSS rules select elements and assign properties. Element, class and id selectors have different specificity; the cascade decides between competing declarations. When specificity and other cascade factors tie, later rules win. Inspect which selector actually matches before adding more overrides.

The note class changes paragraph colour without affecting other elements. The id rule adds bold weight to one paragraph. Rules for different properties can both apply; a winning colour rule does not erase unrelated font-weight.

Practice: Add a warning class with a readable text colour and padding.

Checkpoint: Change one selector at a time and identify the affected elements.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: The note class changes paragraph colour without affecting other elements. The id rule adds bold weight to one paragraph. Rules for different properties can both apply; a winning colour rule does not erase unrelated font-weight.
en.mistake: Avoid scattering important flags to fight an unclear cascade.
en.hint: The note class changes paragraph colour without affecting other elements. The id rule adds bold weight to one paragraph. Rules for different properties can both apply; a winning colour rule does not erase unrelated font-weight.

en.explanation: The note class changes paragraph colour without affecting other elements. The id rule adds bold weight to one paragraph. Rules for different properties can both apply; a winning colour rule does not erase unrelated font-weight.

my.body:
CSS rule သည် selector နှင့် property ဖြင့် element ကို ပြင်သည်။ Element၊ class နှင့် id တို့၏ specificity မတူပါ။ အခြား cascade အချက်များ တူသည့်အခါ နောက်ရေးသော rule က အနိုင်ရသည်။ Selector ကိုက်မကိုက် အရင်စစ်ပါ။

Note class က ဆိုင်သော paragraph များ၏ အရောင်ကို ပြောင်းသည်။ ID rule က တစ်ခုကို bold ထည့်သည်။ Property မတူသော rule များ အတူသက်ရောက်နိုင်ပြီး colour rule နိုင်ခြင်းက font-weight ကို မဖယ်ပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — ဖတ်ရလွယ်သော text colour နှင့် padding ပါသည့် warning class ထည့်ပါ။

en.objectives: Create a 240px border-box card with 16px padding.
en.body:
Every element occupies a box made of content, padding, border and margin. Padding is inside the border; margin separates boxes. With border-box sizing, the declared width includes padding and border, making layouts easier to reason about on narrow screens.

The example remains 220px wide including 40px horizontal padding and 4px border. Under content-box the same declaration would occupy 264px before margins, which can cause unexpected overflow.

Practice: Create a 240px border-box card with 16px padding.

Checkpoint: Draw padding inside the border and margin outside it in your notes.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Add three buttons in a wrapping row with a 12px gap.
en.body:
Flexbox arranges items along a main axis and aligns them on a cross axis. gap provides predictable spacing without margins on every child. Wrapping lets items move to another line when space is limited, but text and controls still need sensible sizes.

justify-content acts along the row and align-items aligns vertically here. These axes change when flex-direction changes, so remember the axis model instead of memorizing horizontal versus vertical.

Practice: Add three buttons in a wrapping row with a 12px gap.

Checkpoint: Use a long button label to reveal whether the row can actually wrap.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: justify-content acts along the row and align-items aligns vertically here. These axes change when flex-direction changes, so remember the axis model instead of memorizing horizontal versus vertical.
en.mistake: Test wrapping with longer Myanmar labels as well as short English words.

en.objectives: Create four subject cards that collapse to one column on a small viewport.
en.body:
Grid describes rows and columns in a layout. auto-fit and minmax can create as many usable columns as space permits. Protect the minimum track size on very narrow screens; otherwise a minimum larger than the viewport forces horizontal overflow.

The minimum is capped at the container width, while 1fr distributes remaining space. Changing preview width demonstrates layout adaptation without needing different HTML for each device.

Practice: Create four subject cards that collapse to one column on a small viewport.

Checkpoint: The grid should not require horizontal scrolling on a narrow preview.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: The minimum is capped at the container width, while 1fr distributes remaining space. Changing preview width demonstrates layout adaptation without needing different HTML for each device.
en.mistake: A fixed wide minimum can break an otherwise responsive grid.

Learning on every screen

Resize the preview.
lessons.solution: <style>article{padding:12px;background:#e2e8f0}@media(min-width:640px){article{padding:30px}}</style><article>Compare narrow and wide screens.</article>

en.objectives: Change card padding above a 640px breakpoint and inspect two preview widths.
en.body:
A mobile-first stylesheet begins with a simple narrow-screen layout and adds changes when enough width is available. A media query tests the viewport, not a specific phone model. Avoid shrinking text to hide overflow; let content wrap and choose a layout that fits.

The base font size is used below 600px; the larger rule applies at or above the breakpoint. Device pixels and CSS pixels are not interchangeable, so reason in CSS viewport units.

Practice: Change card padding above a 640px breakpoint and inspect two preview widths.

Checkpoint: Inspect widths just below and just above the breakpoint as well.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

my.body:
Mobile-first CSS သည် screen ကျဉ်းအတွက် ရိုးရှင်းသော layout ဖြင့် စပြီး အကျယ်ရလာမှ ပြောင်းသည်။ Media query က ဖုန်း model မဟုတ်ဘဲ viewport အကျယ်ကို စစ်သည်။ Overflow ဖျောက်ရန် စာကို အလွန်မသေးပါနှင့်။

600px အောက်တွင် base font ကို သုံးပြီး breakpoint မှစ၍ အကြီးသုံးသည်။ Device pixel နှင့် CSS pixel မတူနိုင်သဖြင့် CSS viewport အပေါ် အခြေခံစဉ်းစားပါ။

en.objectives: Add a readable article and an obvious focus ring to its button.
en.body:
Readability depends on line length, spacing, contrast and focus feedback, not just font choice. A max-width in ch can keep paragraphs comfortable on a large screen. Leave a visible focus indicator so keyboard users know which control will respond to the next action.

The focus-visible selector provides feedback for keyboard-style focus. Good text contrast and flexible spacing should still be tested with zoom and longer content rather than inferred from a single screenshot.

Practice: Add a readable article and an obvious focus ring to its button.

Checkpoint: Use keyboard focus on the button and verify the outline stays visible.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

lessons.code: Waiting
lessons.solution: Loading

en.objectives: Change a paragraph with id status from Loading to Ready.
en.body:
The DOM is the browser representation of the document. JavaScript can select an element and update its properties. A selector may return null when the element is absent or not parsed yet. Put this small script after its target so the element exists before selection.

textContent assigns plain text to the chosen element. It does not interpret the assigned text as HTML markup. Check that selection succeeded before using it when the document structure can vary.

Practice: Change a paragraph with id status from Loading to Ready.

Checkpoint: Remove the target element temporarily to see why a null check matters.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.mistake: Do not assume a selector always finds an element.

TextContent က plain text ကို သတ်မှတ်ပြီး HTML markup အဖြစ် မဖတ်ပါ။ Document ပုံစံ ပြောင်းနိုင်ပါက selector အောင်မြင်မမြင် စစ်ပြီးမှ property သုံးပါ။ Null ကို element ကဲ့သို့ သုံးလျှင် error ဖြစ်နိုင်သည်။

en.objectives: Add a Reset button that sets the counter and displayed text to zero.
en.body:
An event listener connects an interaction to a function. Keep state in a variable and render the current value after changing it. A real button provides keyboard activation and semantics automatically, whereas a clickable div would require extra keyboard and accessibility work.

If Reset changes only the paragraph, the next Add can continue from the old hidden count. Updating state first and using a shared render function keeps the variable and interface consistent.

Practice: Add a Reset button that sets the counter and displayed text to zero.

Checkpoint: Press Add twice, then Reset, then Add once to check state consistency.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.objectives: Change the unit price to 8 and reject negative quantities.
en.body:
Form input values are strings even when an input has numeric controls. Convert intentionally and validate before calculating. For a real currency calculator, define rounding and decimal representation; this small example uses a whole-number unit price to focus on the input and display flow.

Number converts the text and Number.isFinite rejects non-finite results. An empty string converts to zero, so add an explicit empty check when a blank field must not be interpreted as a zero quantity.

Practice: Change the unit price to 8 and reject negative quantities.

Checkpoint: Decide explicitly whether a blank quantity is invalid or represents zero.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.
en.lines: Number converts the text and Number.isFinite rejects non-finite results. An empty string converts to zero, so add an explicit empty check when a blank field must not be interpreted as a zero quantity.

en.objectives: Display a typed message literally, including angle brackets.
en.body:
Use textContent when the requirement is to display user-controlled text. Interpreting that value as markup can turn data into active page content. This principle applies to the text sink shown here; different contexts such as URLs, attributes and script code require their own validation and handling.

The typed angle brackets remain visible characters rather than creating a bold element. The offline preview also has isolation controls, but application code should still use a text sink when HTML is not required.

Practice: Display a typed message literally, including angle brackets.

Checkpoint: The output should display angle brackets without creating a new element.

Try the page at narrow and wide preview widths, then use its controls rather than judging only the initial appearance. Keep labels meaningful and verify that longer text still fits. Saving source restores the source document; it does not automatically preserve temporary interactive state.

en.body:
Combine semantic controls, a responsive container and event-driven rendering into a complete small application. Derive the completed count from the checkboxes rather than storing another count that can drift. This example deliberately keeps state in memory; reloading resets the checklist.

The DOM checkboxes are the source of truth, and the summary is derived from their checked values. No storage or server is used. A saved HTML source file is not the same as saving the current interactive state.

Semantic control၊ responsive container နှင့် event update ကို ပေါင်းပြီး app အသေးတစ်ခု ဆောက်ပါ။ Completed count ကို checkbox များမှ တိုက်ရိုက် တွက်ပါ။ ဤနမူနာသည် memory ထဲသာ ထိန်းသဖြင့် reload လုပ်လျှင် ပြန်စသည်။

en.objectives: Write a scope for one disposable VM that you own.
en.body:
Kali is a security-focused Linux distribution, not a magic shortcut to programming or permission to test other systems. Start by writing a lab scope: ownership, allowed activities, data handling and a stop condition. Keep the learning environment separate from personal accounts and production services.

Tools do not grant authorization. The written scope limits the target and activities before commands are chosen, making it possible to stop when observation reveals a system outside the intended lab.

Practice: Write a scope for one disposable VM that you own.

Checkpoint: Your scope note should say when to stop, not just what tool to run.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: Tools do not grant authorization. The written scope limits the target and activities before commands are chosen, making it possible to stop when observation reveals a system outside the intended lab.
en.mistake: Use an owned or explicitly authorized lab; never infer consent from an open port.
en.hint: Tools do not grant authorization. The written scope limits the target and activities before commands are chosen, making it possible to stop when observation reveals a system outside the intended lab.
en.challenge: Write a scope for one disposable VM that you own.
en.question: Does installing Kali authorize testing a public website?
en.explanation: Tools do not grant authorization. The written scope limits the target and activities before commands are chosen, making it possible to stop when observation reveals a system outside the intended lab.

my.objectives: ကိုယ်ပိုင် စမ်းသပ် VM တစ်လုံးအတွက် scope ရေးပါ။
my.body:
Kali သည် security အတွက် ပြင်ဆင်ထားသော Linux distribution ဖြစ်သည်။ အခြားသူ့စနစ်ကို စမ်းခွင့် အလိုအလျောက် မပေးပါ။ ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု၊ လုပ်ခွင့်၊ data ထိန်းပုံနှင့် ရပ်မည့်အခြေအနေကို lab scope အဖြစ် အရင် ရေးပါ။

Tool ရှိခြင်းက ခွင့်ပြုချက် မဟုတ်ပါ။ Command မရွေးမီ scope က target နှင့် လုပ်ဆောင်မှုကို ကန့်ထားသည်။ Lab ပြင်ပစနစ် ပေါ်လာလျှင် ရပ်နိုင်ရန် stop condition လိုသည်။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — ကိုယ်ပိုင် စမ်းသပ် VM တစ်လုံးအတွက် scope ရေးပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — Scope မှတ်စုတွင် ဘယ်အချိန်ရပ်ရမည်ကိုပါ ရေးပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်မီ လက်ရှိ directory၊ သုံးမည့် tool version နှင့် ကိုယ်ပိုင် lab target ကို တိကျစွာ မှတ်ပါ။ Command နှင့် option တို့၏ တာဝန်ကို အရင်ဖတ်ပြီး တကယ်ထွက်သော output ကိုသာ အထောက်အထား ယူပါ။ ရလဒ်က ဘာကို သက်သေပြပြီး ဘာကို မပြနိုင်သေးသလဲ ခွဲရေးပါ။ စမ်းသပ် folder နှင့် မျှဝေမည့်မှတ်စုတွင် ကိုယ်ရေးအချက်အလက် မထည့်ပါနှင့်။
my.lines: Tool ရှိခြင်းက ခွင့်ပြုချက် မဟုတ်ပါ။ Command မရွေးမီ scope က target နှင့် လုပ်ဆောင်မှုကို ကန့်ထားသည်။ Lab ပြင်ပစနစ် ပေါ်လာလျှင် ရပ်နိုင်ရန် stop condition လိုသည်။

en.objectives: Document the guest network mode and a clean snapshot name.
en.body:
A virtual machine provides a separate guest operating system and a convenient reset point. A snapshot records VM state but is not a complete independent backup strategy. Choose host-only or an isolated lab network for practice; bridged networking can expose a guest to devices on the real local network.

Host-only networking usually provides host-to-guest lab communication without directly bridging the physical LAN. Network modes have different reachability; verify the actual configuration instead of assuming that every VM is isolated.

Practice: Document the guest network mode and a clean snapshot name.

Checkpoint: Keep essential learning notes outside a VM snapshot you plan to roll back.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: Host-only networking usually provides host-to-guest lab communication without directly bridging the physical LAN. Network modes have different reachability; verify the actual configuration instead of assuming that every VM is isolated.
en.mistake: A snapshot rollback can erase unsaved lab notes stored inside the guest.
en.hint: Host-only networking usually provides host-to-guest lab communication without directly bridging the physical LAN. Network modes have different reachability; verify the actual configuration instead of assuming that every VM is isolated.
en.challenge: Document the guest network mode and a clean snapshot name.
en.question: Which network mode directly joins the real LAN?
en.explanation: Host-only networking usually provides host-to-guest lab communication without directly bridging the physical LAN. Network modes have different reachability; verify the actual configuration instead of assuming that every VM is isolated.

my.objectives: Guest network mode နှင့် clean snapshot နာမည် မှတ်ပါ။
my.body:
VM သည် guest OS သီးခြားပေးပြီး snapshot ဖြင့် ပြန်စနိုင်သည်။ Snapshot သည် သီးခြား backup အပြည့်အစုံ မဟုတ်ပါ။ Lab အတွက် host-only သို့မဟုတ် isolated network ရွေးပါ။ Bridged mode က တကယ့် LAN နှင့် guest ကို ချိတ်နိုင်သည်။

Host-only က host နှင့် guest အကြား lab ဆက်သွယ်မှုအတွက် အသုံးများသည်။ Mode များ၏ ရောက်နိုင်သောနေရာ မတူပါ။ VM ဖြစ်ရုံဖြင့် အမြဲ isolated ဟု မယူဆဘဲ configuration ကို တကယ်စစ်ပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — Guest network mode နှင့် clean snapshot နာမည် မှတ်ပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — Rollback လုပ်မည့် VM snapshot ပြင်ပတွင် အရေးကြီးမှတ်စုကို ထိန်းပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်မီ လက်ရှိ directory၊ သုံးမည့် tool version နှင့် ကိုယ်ပိုင် lab target ကို တိကျစွာ မှတ်ပါ။ Command နှင့် option တို့၏ တာဝန်ကို အရင်ဖတ်ပြီး တကယ်ထွက်သော output ကိုသာ အထောက်အထား ယူပါ။ ရလဒ်က ဘာကို သက်သေပြပြီး ဘာကို မပြနိုင်သေးသလဲ ခွဲရေးပါ။ စမ်းသပ် folder နှင့် မျှဝေမည့်မှတ်စုတွင် ကိုယ်ရေးအချက်အလက် မထည့်ပါနှင့်။
my.lines: Host-only က host နှင့် guest အကြား lab ဆက်သွယ်မှုအတွက် အသုံးများသည်။ Mode များ၏ ရောက်နိုင်သောနေရာ မတူပါ။ VM ဖြစ်ရုံဖြင့် အမြဲ isolated ဟု မယူဆဘဲ configuration ကို တကယ်စစ်ပါ။

title.my: Terminal Path နှင့် လက်ရှိနေရာ

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
pwd
printf "Current user: "
whoami
ls -la .
printf "Parent directory: "
realpath ..
lessons.solution:
pwd
ls -la .

en.objectives: Print the current directory and list its entries including hidden names.
en.body:
The terminal has a current working directory. Relative paths are interpreted from that directory, while absolute paths begin at the filesystem root. Check your location before changing files. Hidden names usually begin with a dot; listing them helps explain why a folder is not actually empty.

The dot means the current directory and two dots mean its parent. Shell commands run in the current location unless a path or program option specifies otherwise; verify this before creating your lab folder.

Practice: Print the current directory and list its entries including hidden names.

Checkpoint: Compare an absolute path with a relative path to the same lab file.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The dot means the current directory and two dots mean its parent. Shell commands run in the current location unless a path or program option specifies otherwise; verify this before creating your lab folder.
en.mistake: Do not copy a command before understanding its target path.
en.hint: The dot means the current directory and two dots mean its parent. Shell commands run in the current location unless a path or program option specifies otherwise; verify this before creating your lab folder.
en.challenge: Print the current directory and list its entries including hidden names.
en.question: What does pwd display?
en.explanation: The dot means the current directory and two dots mean its parent. Shell commands run in the current location unless a path or program option specifies otherwise; verify this before creating your lab folder.

my.objectives: လက်ရှိ directory နှင့် hidden name ပါသော စာရင်းကို ပြပါ။
my.body:
Terminal တွင် လက်ရှိ working directory ရှိသည်။ Relative path က ထိုနေရာမှ စပြီး absolute path က filesystem root မှ စသည်။ ဖိုင်ပြောင်းမီ pwd ဖြင့် နေရာစစ်ပါ။ Dot ဖြင့်စသော hidden name များကို ls -a ဖြင့် မြင်နိုင်သည်။

Dot တစ်ခုက လက်ရှိနေရာ၊ နှစ်ခုက parent ကို ဆိုသည်။ Path မသတ်မှတ်လျှင် command သည် လက်ရှိနေရာအပေါ် လုပ်သည်။ ထို့ကြောင့် lab folder မဆောက်မီ နေရာစစ်ရန် အရေးကြီးသည်။

en.objectives: Create a temporary directory and place a note inside it.
en.body:
A disposable workspace keeps practice files away from real projects. mktemp creates a fresh directory rather than assuming a fixed name is unused. Quote path variables so spaces or wildcard characters remain part of the path instead of becoming separate shell arguments.

The directory path is captured from mktemp and reused consistently. Quoting prevents shell word splitting and pathname expansion; it does not make untrusted commands safe or turn the path into an encrypted value.

Practice: Create a temporary directory and place a note inside it.

Checkpoint: A newly created temporary directory avoids overwriting an older named lab.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.

en.objectives: Create four newline-terminated study steps and show the last two.
en.body:
Large files are easier to inspect when output is bounded. head shows the start, tail shows the end, and wc counts lines. Practice with a file you create in the disposable workspace. A line count counts newline delimiters, so an unterminated final line needs careful interpretation.

The file contains three terminated lines, so wc -l reports three. head and tail return selected content without editing the file; output inspection and file mutation are different activities.

Practice: Create four newline-terminated study steps and show the last two.

Checkpoint: Compare a file with a final newline against one without it when counting lines.

en.objectives: Create a lab note readable and writable only by its owner.
en.body:
Unix permissions distinguish the owner, group and others, with read, write and execute bits. Use the least access needed for a task. File permissions do not encrypt file content or protect it from every privileged process; they control access under the operating system permission model.

The owner receives read and write, while group and others receive no access bits. Execute on a directory has a different navigation meaning from execute on a regular file, so do not apply modes blindly across a tree.

Practice: Create a lab note readable and writable only by its owner.

Checkpoint: Permission mode changes should target your practice file, not a shared folder.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The owner receives read and write, while group and others receive no access bits. Execute on a directory has a different navigation meaning from execute on a regular file, so do not apply modes blindly across a tree.
en.mistake: Avoid chmod 777 as a generic fix for permission errors.
en.hint: The owner receives read and write, while group and others receive no access bits. Execute on a directory has a different navigation meaning from execute on a regular file, so do not apply modes blindly across a tree.

en.explanation: The owner receives read and write, while group and others receive no access bits. Execute on a directory has a different navigation meaning from execute on a regular file, so do not apply modes blindly across a tree.

Unix permission တွင် owner၊ group၊ others အတွက် read/write/execute ခွဲသည်။ လိုအပ်သလောက် အနည်းဆုံး ခွင့်ပြုပါ။ Permission သည် ဖိုင်ကို encrypt မလုပ်ဘဲ OS ၏ access စည်းမျဉ်းဖြင့် ထိန်းသည်။

Owner ကို read/write ပေးပြီး group နှင့် others ကို မပေးထားပါ။ Directory ၏ execute သည် လမ်းကြောင်းဝင်နိုင်ခြင်းနှင့် ဆိုင်သဖြင့် regular file နှင့် မတူပါ။ Folder တစ်ခုလုံးကို မသိဘဲ mode မပြောင်းပါနှင့်။

en.objectives: Compare your username, numeric user id and group ids.
en.body:
Processes run with user and group identities. Those identities influence which files and services they can access. Inspect your current identity before diagnosing permission failures. Prefer a normal lab account and elevate only a specific task when there is a clear need.

id shows more than a display name, including group memberships. Effective identity, file modes and other controls can all affect access; changing the visible name does not automatically change those permissions.

Practice: Compare your username, numeric user id and group ids.

Checkpoint: Group membership can explain access even when the displayed username matches.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.

en.objectives: List your own process ids and command names without stopping anything.
en.body:
A process is a running instance of a program. Its PID identifies it during its lifetime, and the same program can have multiple processes. Begin with read-only observation of your own processes. PIDs can be reused after exit, so a recorded PID is not a permanent application identity.

The user filter limits the view to your account, and the output options choose only needed columns. Observing a process does not require killing it; avoid broad termination commands while learning.

Practice: List your own process ids and command names without stopping anything.

Checkpoint: Inspect your shell pid and another owned process without terminating either.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The user filter limits the view to your account, and the output options choose only needed columns. Observing a process does not require killing it; avoid broad termination commands while learning.
en.mistake: Process listings can contain private arguments; share only redacted evidence.
en.hint: The user filter limits the view to your account, and the output options choose only needed columns. Observing a process does not require killing it; avoid broad termination commands while learning.
en.challenge: List your own process ids and command names without stopping anything.

Process သည် မောင်းနေသော program instance ဖြစ်သည်။ PID က သက်တမ်းအတွင်း ခွဲပေးပြီး program တစ်ခုတွင် process များစွာ ရှိနိုင်သည်။ ကိုယ့် process များကို ဖတ်ရှုကြည့်ခြင်းမှ စလေ့လာပါ။

lessons.solution: apt-cache policy nmap

en.objectives: Inspect the candidate and installed versions of nmap without installing it.
en.body:
Kali uses a Debian-style package ecosystem. Inspect package metadata and candidate versions before installing tools. Package names, versions and repository origins are separate facts. Use official configured repositories and read update guidance rather than mixing random third-party package sources.

The policy view reports installed and candidate versions plus sources when metadata is available. Missing metadata does not prove that the package is unsafe or absent everywhere; it may mean the local package lists need maintenance.

Practice: Inspect the candidate and installed versions of nmap without installing it.

Checkpoint: Record the repository origin along with the candidate package version.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The policy view reports installed and candidate versions plus sources when metadata is available. Missing metadata does not prove that the package is unsafe or absent everywhere; it may mean the local package lists need maintenance.
en.mistake: Do not bypass signature checks to make an installation succeed.
en.hint: The policy view reports installed and candidate versions plus sources when metadata is available. Missing metadata does not prove that the package is unsafe or absent everywhere; it may mean the local package lists need maintenance.
en.challenge: Inspect the candidate and installed versions of nmap without installing it.
en.question: Does apt-cache policy install a package?
en.explanation: The policy view reports installed and candidate versions plus sources when metadata is available. Missing metadata does not prove that the package is unsafe or absent everywhere; it may mean the local package lists need maintenance.

my.objectives: Nmap ကို မတင်ဘဲ installed နှင့် candidate version ကို စစ်ပါ။

Policy view က metadata ရှိလျှင် installed/candidate နှင့် source ကို ပြသည်။ Metadata မရှိခြင်းက package မလုံခြုံကြောင်း သက်သေ မဟုတ်ပါ။ Local package list ကို update လုပ်ရန် လိုနေခြင်း ဖြစ်နိုင်သည်။

en.objectives: Count WARN lines in fictional log text using a pipeline.
en.body:
A pipe connects one command output to the next command input. Build a pipeline in stages so you can inspect intermediate results. grep -F treats a pattern as fixed text rather than a regular expression, which is useful when punctuation should be matched literally.

The first stage creates three lines, grep keeps the two INFO lines and wc counts them. A pipeline transforms a stream; it does not automatically edit a source file unless you add a writing operation.

Practice: Count WARN lines in fictional log text using a pipeline.

Checkpoint: Run each pipeline stage separately once before combining the commands.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.

en.objectives: Find regular .md files no more than two levels below the lab folder.
en.body:
find evaluates paths against tests such as type and name. Start from a narrow owned directory and bound depth while learning. Quote a wildcard pattern so find, rather than the shell, interprets it. This command only prints matching paths; it does not delete or change them.

Without quotes, the shell may expand the pattern before find receives it, changing the arguments. The starting dot bounds the search to the current subtree; verify pwd before scanning even an owned filesystem.

Practice: Find regular .md files no more than two levels below the lab folder.

Checkpoint: A wildcard should reach find unchanged, which is why the pattern is quoted.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: Without quotes, the shell may expand the pattern before find receives it, changing the arguments. The starting dot bounds the search to the current subtree; verify pwd before scanning even an owned filesystem.
en.mistake: Do not add deletion actions to a read-only discovery exercise.
en.hint: Without quotes, the shell may expand the pattern before find receives it, changing the arguments. The starting dot bounds the search to the current subtree; verify pwd before scanning even an owned filesystem.
en.challenge: Find regular .md files no more than two levels below the lab folder.
en.question: Why quote "*.txt"?
en.explanation: Without quotes, the shell may expand the pattern before find receives it, changing the arguments. The starting dot bounds the search to the current subtree; verify pwd before scanning even an owned filesystem.

en.objectives: Create a harmless shell variable and print it without listing the full environment.
en.body:
Environment variables pass selected settings to child processes. A shell variable becomes part of a child environment only when exported. Inspect specific non-secret settings rather than dumping every variable; real environments can contain credentials and private endpoint information.

The example prints only chosen settings and a fictional label. Quoting preserves spaces in the value. An exported variable is inherited data, not encryption or a secure credential vault.

Practice: Create a harmless shell variable and print it without listing the full environment.

Checkpoint: Print only a harmless practice variable instead of listing all environment values.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The example prints only chosen settings and a fictional label. Quoting preserves spaces in the value. An exported variable is inherited data, not encryption or a secure credential vault.
en.mistake: Never paste API keys or full environment output into a public issue.

en.objectives: Check whether git is on PATH and print a clear result.
en.body:
Shell assignment uses name=value without spaces around the equals sign. Commands report an exit status, with zero conventionally indicating success. An if statement can test that status directly; it does not need to parse a human-readable message to decide whether a command succeeded.

command -v tests command resolution and its exit status drives the branch. Redirecting the lookup output keeps the exercise focused on the result, without hiding failures from a later actual program run.

Practice: Check whether git is on PATH and print a clear result.

Checkpoint: Check a command lookup status directly rather than matching the printed sentence.

en.objectives: Print three study topics, including one containing spaces.
en.body:
A shell for loop iterates over a sequence of words. Quoting multi-word items keeps each topic together. Start with printing planned actions before changing files in bulk. Names can contain spaces and other unusual characters, so parsing formatted ls output is not a reliable file-iteration method.

The quoted item remains a single argument even though it contains a space. The loop body prints one line per topic. Unquoted expansion can split values and accidentally change the number of iterations.

Practice: Print three study topics, including one containing spaces.

Checkpoint: Quoted multi-word topics should remain one loop item each.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.

en.objectives: List local interface addresses and listening TCP sockets without scanning another host.
en.body:
An interface is a network attachment, an IP address identifies an endpoint within a network context, and a port identifies a transport service endpoint. Read local configuration before choosing a lab target. A listening socket is evidence of a local service, not proof that an external device can reach it.

Loopback points back to the same host. Binding a server to 127.0.0.1 limits it to local IPv4 access, whereas a wildcard bind can listen on additional interfaces subject to other network controls.

Practice: List local interface addresses and listening TCP sockets without scanning another host.

Checkpoint: A listener bound to loopback is different from one bound to a wildcard address.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: Loopback points back to the same host. Binding a server to 127.0.0.1 limits it to local IPv4 access, whereas a wildcard bind can listen on additional interfaces subject to other network controls.
en.mistake: Do not mistake wildcard bind addresses for a remote destination.
en.hint: Loopback points back to the same host. Binding a server to 127.0.0.1 limits it to local IPv4 access, whereas a wildcard bind can listen on additional interfaces subject to other network controls.
en.challenge: List local interface addresses and listening TCP sockets without scanning another host.
en.question: What address is IPv4 loopback?
en.explanation: Loopback points back to the same host. Binding a server to 127.0.0.1 limits it to local IPv4 access, whereas a wildcard bind can listen on additional interfaces subject to other network controls.
