Bind explicitly to loopback and stop the server after practice. This command runs on a computer terminal, not inside the mobile app.

The server remains in the foreground until stopped. Port 8000 must be free; if it is occupied, choose another owned local port and adjust later observations consistently. Do not expose a folder containing keys or personal files.

title.my: ကိုယ်ပိုင် Loopback Lab တွင် Nmap လေ့ကျင့်ခြင်း

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်

lessons.code:
# First start your own loopback server on port 8000.
nmap -sT -p 8000 127.0.0.1
lessons.solution:
nmap -sT -p 8000 127.0.0.1
# Stop your own test server, then repeat the same command.

en.objectives: Observe owned port 8000 before and after stopping your local server.
en.body:
Nmap can observe service reachability within an authorized scope. In this exercise the target is only your own loopback server and the port list contains one known port. A TCP connect scan uses normal connection attempts; it is not a permission bypass and should not be redirected to another target.

An open result means a service accepted connections during observation. A closed or filtered result has a different meaning and does not prove that a device is secure. Record the exact target, port and time with the result.

Practice: Observe owned port 8000 before and after stopping your local server.

Checkpoint: Repeat the same single-port observation after stopping only your test server.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: An open result means a service accepted connections during observation. A closed or filtered result has a different meaning and does not prove that a device is secure. Record the exact target, port and time with the result.
en.mistake: Keep the literal loopback target and the single port for this lesson.
en.hint: An open result means a service accepted connections during observation. A closed or filtered result has a different meaning and does not prove that a device is secure. Record the exact target, port and time with the result.
en.challenge: Observe owned port 8000 before and after stopping your local server.

my.body:

Open ရလဒ်က စမ်းသည့်အချိန် service ချိတ်လက်ခံနေသည်ဟု ဆိုသည်။ Closed သို့ filtered က အဓိပ္ပာယ်မတူပြီး စက်တစ်ခုလုံး လုံခြုံကြောင်း မသက်သေပြပါ။ Target၊ port၊ အချိန်ကို အတူမှတ်ပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — ကိုယ့် test server သာ ရပ်ပြီး single-port observation အတူ ပြန်စမ်းပါ။

title.my: Local HTTP Header ဖတ်ခြင်း

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
# With your own loopback lab running:
curl --head --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8000/
lessons.solution: curl --head --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8000/

en.objectives: Inspect the status line and Content-Type of your owned local page.
en.body:
Headers describe an HTTP response, including media type and other metadata. curl --head requests headers without the ordinary response body, while a timeout prevents an indefinite wait. Some servers handle HEAD differently from GET, so state which request method your observation used.

The output is a transcript from the current local server, not a fixed expected header set. Report the actual values rather than inventing security headers that are not present; the simple teaching server has limited behavior.

Practice: Inspect the status line and Content-Type of your owned local page.

Checkpoint: A HEAD response documents headers for that method at the observed time.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The output is a transcript from the current local server, not a fixed expected header set. Report the actual values rather than inventing security headers that are not present; the simple teaching server has limited behavior.
en.mistake: A server header alone does not establish a verified software version.
en.hint: The output is a transcript from the current local server, not a fixed expected header set. Report the actual values rather than inventing security headers that are not present; the simple teaching server has limited behavior.
en.challenge: Inspect the status line and Content-Type of your owned local page.
en.question: Which method does curl --head normally request?
en.explanation: The output is a transcript from the current local server, not a fixed expected header set. Report the actual values rather than inventing security headers that are not present; the simple teaching server has limited behavior.

my.objectives: ကိုယ်ပိုင် local page ၏ status line နှင့် Content-Type ကို ဖတ်ပါ။
my.body:
Header သည် HTTP response ၏ media type နှင့် metadata ကို ဖော်ပြသည်။ Curl --head က ပုံမှန် body မယူဘဲ header တောင်းပြီး timeout က အကြာကြီး စောင့်ခြင်းကို ကန့်သည်။ HEAD နှင့် GET ကို server က မတူကိုင်တွယ်နိုင်သည်။

Output သည် လက်ရှိ local server မှ တကယ့်ရလဒ်ဖြစ်ပြီး ကြိုသတ်မှတ် header စာရင်း မဟုတ်ပါ။ မပါသော security header ကို မရှိဘဲ ရှိသည်ဟု မရေးပါနှင့်။ Teaching server ၏ အလုပ်လုပ်ပုံမှာ ကန့်သတ်ချက် ရှိသည်။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — HEAD ရလဒ်က စမ်းသည့်အချိန် ထို method ၏ header ကိုသာ ဖော်ပြသည်။

title.my: ကိုယ်ပိုင် Packet Capture ဖတ်ခြင်း

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
# Use a capture file created in your own isolated lab.
# lab.pcap is not bundled with the app.
tshark -r lab.pcap -c 5 -Y "http.request"
lessons.solution: tshark -r lab.pcap -c 5 -Y "http.request"

en.objectives: Inspect at most five HTTP requests from an owned lab.pcap file.
en.body:
A packet capture is a record of observed network traffic. This lesson reads an existing owned lab capture rather than collecting other people’s traffic. Display filters select what is shown, and a row limit keeps the first inspection manageable. Capture files may contain sensitive payloads and identifiers.

The -r option chooses offline input and -Y applies a display filter. Encrypted HTTPS payloads are not automatically readable as HTTP messages; a capture is not a universal decryption tool.

Practice: Inspect at most five HTTP requests from an owned lab.pcap file.

Checkpoint: Keep the source capture private even if the filtered display looks harmless.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.
en.lines: The -r option chooses offline input and -Y applies a display filter. Encrypted HTTPS payloads are not automatically readable as HTTP messages; a capture is not a universal decryption tool.
en.mistake: Do not upload real captures publicly; create fictional lab evidence.
en.hint: The -r option chooses offline input and -Y applies a display filter. Encrypted HTTPS payloads are not automatically readable as HTTP messages; a capture is not a universal decryption tool.
en.challenge: Inspect at most five HTTP requests from an owned lab.pcap file.
en.question: What does -r lab.pcap do?
en.explanation: The -r option chooses offline input and -Y applies a display filter. Encrypted HTTPS payloads are not automatically readable as HTTP messages; a capture is not a universal decryption tool.

my.body:
Packet capture သည် network traffic မှတ်တမ်းဖြစ်သည်။ ဤသင်ခန်းစာက ကိုယ်ပိုင် isolated lab မှ ဖိုင်ကို ဖတ်ခြင်းသာ ဖြစ်ပြီး အခြားသူ့ traffic မဖမ်းပါ။ Display filter က မြင်ရမည့် record ရွေးသည်။ Capture ထဲ sensitive data ပါနိုင်သည်။

-r က offline ဖိုင်ကို ရွေးပြီး -Y က display filter သတ်မှတ်သည်။ HTTPS encrypted payload ကို HTTP စာသားအဖြစ် အလိုအလျောက် မဖတ်နိုင်ပါ။ Capture ရှိခြင်းက decrypt လုပ်နိုင်သည်ဟု မဆိုလိုပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — ကိုယ်ပိုင် lab.pcap မှ HTTP request ငါးခုအများဆုံး ဖတ်ပါ။

en.objectives: Write an observation, an uncertainty and a next verification step for the WARN event.
en.body:
Triage separates observation from explanation and remediation. Record the relevant event, timestamp and context, then state what remains uncertain. A warning line is a clue, not proof of an attack. Use fictional logs for practice so the reporting process does not disclose real users or tokens.

grep -n reports a line number alongside the matching event. Preserve the original fictional file so another learner can reproduce your observation, and keep your inference separate from the raw event.

Practice: Write an observation, an uncertainty and a next verification step for the WARN event.

Checkpoint: Keep the raw fictional event separate from your explanation of its cause.

Record the working directory, relevant tool version and the exact owned lab target before practice. Read the command and its options first, observe the actual output, and explain what the result does and does not establish. Keep personal data out of the disposable lab and shared notes.

lessons.code:
Scope -> Baseline -> Observe -> Explain -> Fix -> Retest
Target: owned localhost lab
Evidence: fictional requests only
Deliverable: reproducible finding and verified fix
lessons.solution:
Scope: 127.0.0.1 owned page
Baseline: expected status and content
Observation: compare actual status and content
Fix: change only the owned page
Retest: repeat the same request

en.objectives: Plan a read-only assessment of your owned loopback page.
en.body:
An ethical assessment is a controlled investigation with permission and a clear goal. Establish normal behavior before interpreting unusual results. A useful finding explains the affected behavior, evidence, impact and a fix that can be retested. Tool output alone is not a complete assessment.

Writing the scope first distinguishes legitimate lab work from unauthorized testing. Baseline and retest use comparable conditions, so the report can show whether the proposed fix actually changed the observed behavior.

Practice: Plan a read-only assessment of your owned loopback page.

Checkpoint: A baseline should be reproducible under the same owned lab conditions.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: Writing the scope first distinguishes legitimate lab work from unauthorized testing. Baseline and retest use comparable conditions, so the report can show whether the proposed fix actually changed the observed behavior.
en.mistake: Never expand a test scope merely because another host is reachable.

Scope အရင်ရေးခြင်းက ခွင့်ပြု lab အလုပ်ကို ခွဲပေးသည်။ Baseline နှင့် retest ကို အခြေအနေတူစမ်းမှ ပြင်ဆင်ချက်က တွေ့ရှိသော behavior ကို တကယ်ပြောင်းမပြောင်း သိနိုင်သည်။

Control တစ်ခုစီအတွက် ကာကွယ်လိုသော asset နှင့် စစ်ဆေးရမည့် boundary ကို အမည်တပ်ပါ။ နမူနာ data ဖြင့် ခွင့်ရှိသောအခြေအနေနှင့် ခွင့်မရှိသောအခြေအနေ နှစ်မျိုးလုံး စမ်းပြီး တကယ့်ရလဒ်ကို မှတ်ပါ။ နမူနာတစ်ခု မှန်ကန်ခြင်းက ထို behavior ကိုသာ ထောက်ခံပြီး app တစ်ခုလုံး အားနည်းချက်မရှိကြောင်း လက်မှတ် မဟုတ်ပါ။

Logs: identifiers without secrets

Assets: note text, login session, backup

en.objectives: Identify three assets and two trust checks in a note-taking application.
en.body:
Threat modeling starts with what you need to protect and where trust changes. Draw the data flow and identify entry points, sensitive assets and assumptions. A trust boundary is not necessarily a machine boundary: two user accounts on the same API can still require strict separation.

The API must validate identity and ownership before selecting private rows. A client-provided owner id is data from outside the boundary; it cannot establish permission by itself.

Practice: Identify three assets and two trust checks in a note-taking application.

Checkpoint: Mark user-controlled input arrows on the data-flow sketch.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: The API must validate identity and ownership before selecting private rows. A client-provided owner id is data from outside the boundary; it cannot establish permission by itself.
en.mistake: A diagram documents assumptions; it does not enforce them.
en.hint: The API must validate identity and ownership before selecting private rows. A client-provided owner id is data from outside the boundary; it cannot establish permission by itself.

en.question: Which is a trust-boundary check?
en.explanation: The API must validate identity and ownership before selecting private rows. A client-provided owner id is data from outside the boundary; it cannot establish permission by itself.

en.objectives: Map an owner check, a checksum and a tested backup to their primary goals.
en.body:
Confidentiality limits unauthorized disclosure, integrity protects against unauthorized or incorrect changes, and availability concerns usable access when needed. These goals overlap but are not interchangeable. Encryption can help confidentiality while a backup and restore process may be essential for availability.

A tested restore can recover usable data after loss. A checksum detects differences when the expected checksum is trusted; it does not hide the data or prove that the original author was legitimate.

Practice: Map an owner check, a checksum and a tested backup to their primary goals.

Checkpoint: A backup is useful only when its recovery path is understood and tested.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A tested restore can recover usable data after loss. A checksum detects differences when the expected checksum is trusted; it does not hide the data or prove that the original author was legitimate.
en.mistake: Name the security goal before choosing a control.

en.objectives: Add a reviewer role that can view and comment but cannot edit.
en.body:
Least privilege gives an identity only the capabilities needed for its task. Separate ordinary reading, content editing and administration rather than using a universal administrator role. Check permissions at the action boundary; hiding a button is a convenience, not authorization enforcement.

The reader lacks edit permission, so the example returns False. The same check must be enforced where state changes occur. A caller can otherwise invoke an endpoint directly without using the interface.

Practice: Add a reviewer role that can view and comment but cannot edit.

Checkpoint: An unknown role should receive no default write permissions.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: The reader lacks edit permission, so the example returns False. The same check must be enforced where state changes occur. A caller can otherwise invoke an endpoint directly without using the interface.
en.mistake: Default-deny unknown roles rather than treating them as administrators.

lessons.solution:
def can_read(user_id, owner_id):
    return user_id is not None and user_id == owner_id

assert can_read("a","a")
assert not can_read("b","a")
assert not can_read(None,"a")
print("ownership cases passed")

en.objectives: Test own, other-user and signed-out access using the pure function.
en.body:
Authentication establishes who a caller is; authorization decides whether that caller may perform an action on a resource. Logging in does not grant access to every record. Use the authenticated identity to enforce ownership, and test with at least two independent accounts in an owned test environment.

The first call returns True and the second False. The function is a small model, not a full login system; a real service must derive user_id from a verified session rather than trusting a submitted string.

Practice: Test own, other-user and signed-out access using the pure function.

Checkpoint: Test ownership checks with two accounts, not two records owned by one account.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: The first call returns True and the second False. The function is a small model, not a full login system; a real service must derive user_id from a verified session rather than trusting a submitted string.
en.mistake: Never authorize solely from a client-supplied owner field.
en.hint: The first call returns True and the second False. The function is a small model, not a full login system; a real service must derive user_id from a verified session rather than trusting a submitted string.

lessons.solution:
def valid_title(value):
    return isinstance(value,str) and 1 <= len(value.strip()) <= 80

print(valid_title("Loops"))
print(valid_title("   "))

en.objectives: Accept a lesson title only when it is nonblank text of at most 80 characters.
en.body:
Validation defines the accepted data contract. Check type, range, length and allowed structure close to the entry boundary. Reject invalid data explicitly rather than silently converting every value. Normalize only when the transformation is part of the documented contract and does not hide meaning.

In Python bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True. The stricter check rejects a Boolean when the contract requires a genuine numeric score instead of treating True as one.

Practice: Accept a lesson title only when it is nonblank text of at most 80 characters.

Checkpoint: Boundary values zero and one hundred are valid in this score contract.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.

en.mistake: Input validation does not replace contextual output encoding or authorization.

en.objectives: Encode a fictional note containing < and & for an HTML text context.
en.body:
Output encoding keeps data from being interpreted as active syntax in a particular destination. HTML text, HTML attributes, JavaScript and URLs are different contexts. Choose a safe API or context-appropriate encoder instead of assuming that one escape function protects every possible use.

The angle brackets become character references in the output. That is appropriate for displaying literal text in HTML, but inserting this result into executable script is a different operation requiring a different design.

Practice: Encode a fictional note containing < and & for an HTML text context.

Checkpoint: Keep text, attribute, URL and script destinations distinct in the design.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.

en.objectives: Insert and retrieve a fictional learner name containing an apostrophe.
en.body:
Parameterized queries separate SQL structure from data values. The database driver handles the value representation, including apostrophes, without constructing SQL through string concatenation. Parameters usually stand for values, not arbitrary table names or column identifiers; choose identifiers from a fixed allowlist when necessary.

The single-element tuple needs a trailing comma. The query template stays fixed while the apostrophe-bearing value is bound separately. A successful example demonstrates value handling, not a full database authorization model.

Practice: Insert and retrieve a fictional learner name containing an apostrophe.

Checkpoint: A value with an apostrophe should remain ordinary data after binding.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.

lessons.code:
Use a maintained password-hashing library.
Registration: password -> unique salt + slow password hash
Storage: algorithm, parameters, salt, hash
Login: library verification against stored record
Never store plaintext passwords or use a fast unsalted digest.
lessons.solution:
Register: validate input -> library hash -> save hash record
Login: load hash record -> library verify -> create session
Logs: success/failure only, never password

en.objectives: Write a registration and login flow that never persists the raw password.
en.body:
Passwords need purpose-built slow password hashing with a unique salt and maintained library support. A general fast hash such as SHA-256 is not a complete password storage design. Store the parameters needed for verification, support upgrades, and keep the raw password out of logs and analytics.

A salt makes identical passwords produce distinct stored records, while a password-hashing cost slows guessing. These solve different problems; a salt alone does not turn a fast general hash into an appropriate password-hashing scheme.

Practice: Write a registration and login flow that never persists the raw password.

Checkpoint: Password verification should use the maintained library matching the stored format.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A salt makes identical passwords produce distinct stored records, while a password-hashing cost slows guessing. These solve different problems; a salt alone does not turn a fast general hash into an appropriate password-hashing scheme.
en.mistake: Do not invent your own cryptographic password protocol.
en.hint: A salt makes identical passwords produce distinct stored records, while a password-hashing cost slows guessing. These solve different problems; a salt alone does not turn a fast general hash into an appropriate password-hashing scheme.
en.challenge: Write a registration and login flow that never persists the raw password.
en.question: Is plain SHA-256 enough for password storage?
en.explanation: A salt makes identical passwords produce distinct stored records, while a password-hashing cost slows guessing. These solve different problems; a salt alone does not turn a fast general hash into an appropriate password-hashing scheme.

my.objectives: Raw password မသိမ်းသော registration/login flow ရေးပါ။
my.body:
Password ကို unique salt နှင့် purpose-built slow hashing library ဖြင့် သိမ်းရသည်။ SHA-256 ကဲ့သို့ fast hash တစ်ခုတည်းသည် password storage design မပြည့်စုံပါ။ Verification parameter များ ထိန်းပြီး password အစစ်ကို log မလုပ်ပါနှင့်။

Salt က password တူလျှင် stored record မတူစေပြီး hashing cost က guessing အလုပ်ကို နှေးစေသည်။ တာဝန်နှစ်ခု မတူပါ။ Salt ထည့်ရုံဖြင့် fast hash သည် သင့်တော်သော password hashing မဖြစ်ပါ။

title.my: MFA နှင့် Recovery Code

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
Account protection plan
Password: unique and stored in a password manager
Second factor: use the provider-supported option
Recovery: store codes privately, separate from the device
Support: use official account recovery only
lessons.solution:
Enable supported MFA
Store recovery codes in a private safe location
Record the official recovery route
Review connected devices periodically

en.objectives: Create a private recovery checklist without writing actual codes into the app.
en.body:
Multi-factor authentication combines different kinds of proof, such as a password and a possession factor. Recovery is part of the design: losing a phone should not lead to insecure improvised bypasses. Treat recovery codes as credentials, and never send them to a person claiming to be support in a message.

An attacker who obtains a recovery code may be able to use it in the provider recovery flow. A second factor adds protection, but phishing resistance and recovery behavior depend on the specific method and service.

Practice: Create a private recovery checklist without writing actual codes into the app.

Checkpoint: Recovery instructions should point to the actual official account service.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: An attacker who obtains a recovery code may be able to use it in the provider recovery flow. A second factor adds protection, but phishing resistance and recovery behavior depend on the specific method and service.
en.mistake: Do not practice with real recovery codes in screenshots or shared lessons.
en.hint: An attacker who obtains a recovery code may be able to use it in the provider recovery flow. A second factor adds protection, but phishing resistance and recovery behavior depend on the specific method and service.
en.challenge: Create a private recovery checklist without writing actual codes into the app.
en.question: How should recovery codes be treated?
en.explanation: An attacker who obtains a recovery code may be able to use it in the provider recovery flow. A second factor adds protection, but phishing resistance and recovery behavior depend on the specific method and service.

my.objectives: Code အစစ်မထည့်ဘဲ private recovery checklist ရေးပါ။
my.body:
MFA သည် password နှင့် ပစ္စည်းပိုင်ဆိုင်မှုကဲ့သို့ proof မတူသည်များ ပေါင်းသုံးသည်။ ဖုန်းပျောက်လျှင် လုံခြုံသော recovery ရှိရန် ကြိုစီစဉ်ပါ။ Recovery code သည် credential ဖြစ်သဖြင့် support ဟု ပြောသောသူထံ မပို့ပါနှင့်။

Recovery code ရသူက provider recovery flow တွင် သုံးနိုင်သည်။ Second factor သည် ကာကွယ်မှုတိုးသော်လည်း phishing ခံနိုင်ရည်နှင့် recovery behavior သည် method နှင့် service အလိုက် မတူပါ။

lessons.solution:
provider="example"
has_key=True

en.objectives: Create a diagnostic record showing provider and whether a key exists, without its value.
en.body:
A secret should reach only the component that needs it. Keep real credentials out of source control, screenshots and logs. A mobile BYOK app may store a user-supplied key in protected device storage, but a server-owned key belongs on the server. Document exactly where a key is sent.

The safe log contains a Boolean rather than the credential. Redaction should be designed before errors occur; exception messages and upstream response bodies can otherwise accidentally echo a secret.

Practice: Create a diagnostic record showing provider and whether a key exists, without its value.

Checkpoint: Credential redaction applies to exception and upstream response messages too.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: The safe log contains a Boolean rather than the credential. Redaction should be designed before errors occur; exception messages and upstream response bodies can otherwise accidentally echo a secret.
en.mistake: Do not assume deleting a leaked key from Git revokes it at the provider.
en.hint: The safe log contains a Boolean rather than the credential. Redaction should be designed before errors occur; exception messages and upstream response bodies can otherwise accidentally echo a secret.

Secret ကို လိုအပ်သော component သို့သာ ပို့ပါ။ Key အစစ်ကို source၊ screenshot နှင့် log ထဲ မထည့်ပါနှင့်။ BYOK key ကို device protected storage တွင် ထိန်းနိုင်သော်လည်း server-owned key သည် server ပေါ်တွင်သာ ရှိသင့်သည်။

lessons.code:
Client -> verify certificate and hostname -> encrypted connection
Do: use supported HTTPS clients with verification enabled
Do: handle certificate failure explicitly
Do not: disable verification to hide an error
lessons.solution:
Check 1: trusted certificate chain
Check 2: certificate matches requested hostname
Then use the verified encrypted connection

en.objectives: List the two transport checks a client needs before sending a private token.
en.body:
HTTPS protects data in transit when the certificate chain and hostname are verified. It does not prove that the application is honest or that stored data is secure. Treat a certificate error as a configuration or trust issue to investigate rather than bypassing verification to make a request succeed.

Encryption without authenticating the endpoint can protect traffic to the wrong party. Local plain-HTTP loopback exercises are a separate teaching context and should not be copied as production token transport settings.

Practice: List the two transport checks a client needs before sending a private token.

Checkpoint: Hostname verification is separate from successfully encrypting a connection.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: Encryption without authenticating the endpoint can protect traffic to the wrong party. Local plain-HTTP loopback exercises are a separate teaching context and should not be copied as production token transport settings.
en.mistake: A lock icon does not certify an application security audit.
en.hint: Encryption without authenticating the endpoint can protect traffic to the wrong party. Local plain-HTTP loopback exercises are a separate teaching context and should not be copied as production token transport settings.

lessons.code:
Session lifecycle
Create after verified login
Rotate after sensitive identity changes
Check expiry and authorization on requests
Invalidate according to logout policy
Never include session tokens in URLs or logs
lessons.solution:
Local logout: remove this device session as designed
All-device logout: revoke relevant server sessions
Both: stop sending old credentials and handle expiry

en.objectives: Describe local logout versus logout on all devices.
en.body:
A session connects multiple requests to an authenticated identity. Tokens need bounded lifetimes and server-side validation appropriate to the design. Logout behavior must be explicit: removing a local token and revoking a server session are related but different actions, especially across multiple devices.

A local operation may stop this app from making future requests while other devices still hold valid sessions. The user-facing wording must match the actual revocation behavior rather than promising a broader logout.

Practice: Describe local logout versus logout on all devices.

Checkpoint: Document whether logout affects this device or all server sessions.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A local operation may stop this app from making future requests while other devices still hold valid sessions. The user-facing wording must match the actual revocation behavior rather than promising a broader logout.
en.mistake: Never treat a decoded but unverified token as an authenticated session.
en.hint: A local operation may stop this app from making future requests while other devices still hold valid sessions. The user-facing wording must match the actual revocation behavior rather than promising a broader logout.
en.challenge: Describe local logout versus logout on all devices.
en.question: Does deleting one local token always revoke every server session?
en.explanation: A local operation may stop this app from making future requests while other devices still hold valid sessions. The user-facing wording must match the actual revocation behavior rather than promising a broader logout.

flow: Read / ဖတ်

lessons.code:
Set-Cookie: session=FICTIONAL; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
Use HTTPS in production.
Choose domain and lifetime deliberately.
Validate the session and authorization on the server.
lessons.solution:
Secure: secure transport
HttpOnly: no normal document.cookie access
SameSite: cross-site sending rules
Path: request-path scope, not an authorization boundary

en.objectives: Explain the purpose of each flag in the fictional header.
en.body:
Cookie flags reduce particular browser risks. Secure limits transmission to secure channels, HttpOnly blocks normal document-script access, and SameSite influences cross-site sending. None of these replaces session validation or output safety, and the right SameSite setting depends on the application flow.

HttpOnly reduces direct cookie reading by page scripts, but malicious scripts can still act through a compromised page in other ways. Path limits cookie sending; it is not a complete resource access-control mechanism.

Practice: Explain the purpose of each flag in the fictional header.

Checkpoint: Cookie Path is a sending rule and does not prove resource ownership.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: HttpOnly reduces direct cookie reading by page scripts, but malicious scripts can still act through a compromised page in other ways. Path limits cookie sending; it is not a complete resource access-control mechanism.
en.mistake: Do not put a real session value into the lesson or a screenshot.
en.hint: HttpOnly reduces direct cookie reading by page scripts, but malicious scripts can still act through a compromised page in other ways. Path limits cookie sending; it is not a complete resource access-control mechanism.
en.challenge: Explain the purpose of each flag in the fictional header.
en.question: Which flag restricts normal JavaScript cookie access?
en.explanation: HttpOnly reduces direct cookie reading by page scripts, but malicious scripts can still act through a compromised page in other ways. Path limits cookie sending; it is not a complete resource access-control mechanism.

Cookie flag များက browser risk တချို့ကို လျှော့သည်။ Secure က secure channel သုံးစေပြီး HttpOnly က document script မှ ပုံမှန်ဖတ်ခြင်းကို တားသည်။ SameSite က cross-site ပို့ပုံကို ထိန်းသည်။ Server session check ကို အစားမထိုးပါ။

HttpOnly က page script မှ cookie ဖတ်ခြင်းကို လျှော့သော်လည်း မကောင်းသော script က page မှတစ်ဆင့် အခြားလုပ်ဆောင်မှု လုပ်နိုင်သေးသည်။ Path သည် cookie ပို့သည့်နေရာကို ကန့်ခြင်းဖြစ်ပြီး authorization မဟုတ်ပါ။

title.my: CSRF နှင့် State ပြောင်းသော Request

flow: Read / ဖတ်
Trace / လိုက်ကြည့်
Practice / လေ့ကျင့်
lessons.code:
State-changing action
1. Authenticate the session.
2. Verify the action is authorized.
3. Enforce the framework CSRF protection where needed.
4. Validate input and record the result.
GET requests should not silently change account settings.
lessons.solution:
POST change-email
Verified session
Authorized owner
Verified CSRF protection for cookie authentication
Validated email and confirmation policy

en.objectives: Write checks for a fictional change-email action without real credentials.
en.body:
Cross-site request forgery exploits a browser automatically attaching credentials to an unwanted request. Use the framework protection suited to your authentication design, such as verified CSRF tokens and appropriate origin checks. SameSite can help but should be evaluated alongside the complete application flow.

A state-changing GET can be triggered unintentionally by navigation or automated fetching. Method choice alone is not a full CSRF defense; the server still needs the appropriate token, origin and session protections.

Practice: Write checks for a fictional change-email action without real credentials.

Checkpoint: A state-changing request still needs identity and ownership checks after CSRF checks.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A state-changing GET can be triggered unintentionally by navigation or automated fetching. Method choice alone is not a full CSRF defense; the server still needs the appropriate token, origin and session protections.
en.mistake: Use established framework mechanisms rather than a home-made token check.
en.hint: A state-changing GET can be triggered unintentionally by navigation or automated fetching. Method choice alone is not a full CSRF defense; the server still needs the appropriate token, origin and session protections.
en.challenge: Write checks for a fictional change-email action without real credentials.
en.question: Which action should avoid being implemented as a simple GET link?
en.explanation: A state-changing GET can be triggered unintentionally by navigation or automated fetching. Method choice alone is not a full CSRF defense; the server still needs the appropriate token, origin and session protections.

my.objectives: နမူနာ change-email action အတွက် credential အစစ်မပါသော check list ရေးပါ။
my.body:
CSRF တွင် browser က credential ကို အလိုအလျောက် ထည့်ပို့ခြင်းကို မလိုလားသော request အတွက် အသုံးချသည်။ Framework ၏ CSRF protection နှင့် သင့်တော်သော origin check ကို သုံးပါ။ SameSite တစ်ခုတည်းကို flow မစစ်ဘဲ မမှီပါနှင့်။

State ပြောင်းသော GET ကို navigation သို့ automated fetch က မရည်ရွယ်ဘဲ ခေါ်နိုင်သည်။ Method ရွေးရုံက CSRF ကာကွယ်မှုအပြည့် မဟုတ်ဘဲ server တွင် token၊ origin နှင့် session ကာကွယ်မှု လိုသေးသည်။

title.my: CORS သည် Authorization မဟုတ်ခြင်း

lessons.code:
Browser policy: may this origin read this cross-origin response?
API authorization: may this identity access this resource?
These are separate questions.
Restrict allowed origins deliberately and still verify every private request.
lessons.solution:
Origin rule: approved web frontend may read responses
Access rule: authenticated user may read only owned notes
Apply both independently

en.objectives: Separate a browser-origin rule from an owner-only data access rule.
en.body:
CORS controls browser cross-origin response sharing. It is not a login system and does not prevent a non-browser client from calling an endpoint. Configure allowed origins and credential behavior carefully, while enforcing authentication and resource authorization on the API regardless of CORS.

A browser may block a page from reading a response, but the server still receives requests from other clients. Resource ownership must therefore be checked independently instead of treating an origin header as a user identity.

Practice: Separate a browser-origin rule from an owner-only data access rule.

Checkpoint: A non-browser client is not governed by the browser CORS read policy.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A browser may block a page from reading a response, but the server still receives requests from other clients. Resource ownership must therefore be checked independently instead of treating an origin header as a user identity.
en.mistake: A wildcard origin is not a substitute for a deliberate access policy.
en.hint: A browser may block a page from reading a response, but the server still receives requests from other clients. Resource ownership must therefore be checked independently instead of treating an origin header as a user identity.
en.challenge: Separate a browser-origin rule from an owner-only data access rule.
en.question: Can a private API rely only on CORS?

lessons.code:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'
Illustrative production policy only.
Adapt script, style and resource rules to the actual app.
Validate first using the supported reporting workflow.
lessons.solution:
default-src: fallback source policy
object-src 'none': block plugin objects
base-uri 'none': disallow base element URLs

en.objectives: Explain default-src, object-src and base-uri without copying the sample blindly.
en.body:
CSP lets a browser restrict resource sources and certain active behaviors. A policy must match the application design and be tested for breakage. It is a defense-in-depth control, not a replacement for safe DOM APIs or contextual output encoding. The learning viewer uses a separate intentionally isolated policy.

default-src is a fallback for relevant fetch directives, not every directive. base-uri therefore deserves its own explicit rule. A copied policy that breaks essential scripts is not a completed security improvement.

Practice: Explain default-src, object-src and base-uri without copying the sample blindly.

Checkpoint: Test a proposed CSP against the app before claiming the deployment works.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: default-src is a fallback for relevant fetch directives, not every directive. base-uri therefore deserves its own explicit rule. A copied policy that breaks essential scripts is not a completed security improvement.
en.mistake: Do not weaken the production app policy merely to run an untrusted preview.
en.hint: default-src is a fallback for relevant fetch directives, not every directive. base-uri therefore deserves its own explicit rule. A copied policy that breaks essential scripts is not a completed security improvement.

en.question: Is CSP a replacement for safe output handling?
en.explanation: default-src is a fallback for relevant fetch directives, not every directive. base-uri therefore deserves its own explicit rule. A copied policy that breaks essential scripts is not a completed security improvement.

title.my: Dependency စာရင်းနှင့် Update စစ်ခြင်း

lessons.code:
Inventory: package name, locked version, source, purpose
Review: official advisory and compatibility notes

en.objectives: Create an inventory row and a validation plan for one fictional package update.
en.body:
Dependencies bring both functionality and maintenance responsibilities. A lockfile makes a resolved version set repeatable, but does not establish that every dependency is secure. Review relevant advisories, update deliberately and rerun meaningful checks. Avoid blindly replacing the entire stack when one focused update addresses the issue.

The inventory explains why a package is present and what changed. Verification should exercise the workflow affected by the update, because a successful install alone says nothing about application behavior.

Practice: Create an inventory row and a validation plan for one fictional package update.

Checkpoint: Record both the reason for an update and the behavior that was verified afterward.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.

en.mistake: Do not silence a relevant advisory without understanding exposure and mitigation.

en.objectives: Write a fictional denied-access event with no password, token or note text.
en.body:
Logs should support diagnosis and accountability without creating a second store of secrets. Record a meaningful action, outcome and correlation identifier. Avoid raw passwords, access tokens and full private request bodies. Define retention and access rules rather than keeping every event forever.

The request id connects related events without copying private content. A denied result documents what happened; it does not reveal whether a particular private note exists to an unauthorized user.

Practice: Write a fictional denied-access event with no password, token or note text.

Checkpoint: An event outcome can be useful without recording a private message body.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: The request id connects related events without copying private content. A denied result documents what happened; it does not reveal whether a particular private note exists to an unauthorized user.
en.mistake: Redact before persistence, not only when showing the log on screen.
en.hint: The request id connects related events without copying private content. A denied result documents what happened; it does not reveal whether a particular private note exists to an unauthorized user.

lessons.code:
Owned lab finding
Observation: another test account could read a fictional note
Expected: only its owner can read it
Fix: enforce verified owner at the server boundary
Retest: owner succeeds, other account and signed-out caller fail
Report: minimal redacted evidence through the approved channel
lessons.solution:
Observation: unauthorized fictional-note read
Impact: ownership boundary failed in the lab
Fix: server verifies caller ownership
Retest: owner allowed; other user denied; signed-out denied
Evidence: redacted requests and actual responses

en.objectives: Write a lab report with observation, impact, fix and three retest cases.
en.body:
A responsible finding report is precise, bounded and reproducible. Explain expected versus actual behavior with minimal fictional evidence. For systems outside your own lab, follow the explicitly published reporting and authorization rules. Do not collect extra private data to make a finding appear more serious.

A retest checks the original failure and nearby allowed and denied cases. Hiding an interface control would not repair direct API access. Report remaining uncertainty instead of claiming a complete system audit from one repaired lab behavior.

Practice: Write a lab report with observation, impact, fix and three retest cases.

Checkpoint: Retest both the original denied case and a legitimate allowed case after a fix.

For each control, name the asset and the boundary where enforcement belongs. Use fictional data to check an allowed case and a denied case, then record the actual results. A passing example supports that specific behavior; it is not a certificate that an entire application has no weaknesses.
en.lines: A retest checks the original failure and nearby allowed and denied cases. Hiding an interface control would not repair direct API access. Report remaining uncertainty instead of claiming a complete system audit from one repaired lab behavior.
en.mistake: Do not publish private evidence or test outside the approved scope.
en.hint: A retest checks the original failure and nearby allowed and denied cases. Hiding an interface control would not repair direct API access. Report remaining uncertainty instead of claiming a complete system audit from one repaired lab behavior.
en.challenge: Write a lab report with observation, impact, fix and three retest cases.
en.question: When is the fix supported by stronger evidence?
en.explanation: A retest checks the original failure and nearby allowed and denied cases. Hiding an interface control would not repair direct API access. Report remaining uncertainty instead of claiming a complete system audit from one repaired lab behavior.

my.objectives: Observation၊ impact၊ fix နှင့် retest သုံးခုပါသော lab report ရေးပါ။

Retest သည် မူလ failure နှင့် allowed/denied အခြေအနေများကို စစ်သည်။ UI ခလုတ်ဖျောက်ခြင်းက direct API access ကို မပြင်နိုင်ပါ။ Lab behavior တစ်ခု ပြင်ပြီးနောက် system audit အပြည့် ပြီးသည်ဟု မဆိုဘဲ ကျန်မသေချာမှု ရေးပါ။

လေ့ကျင့်ရန် — Observation၊ impact၊ fix နှင့် retest သုံးခုပါသော lab report ရေးပါ။

ထပ်မံစစ်ဆေးရန် — Fix ပြီးနောက် မူလ denied case နှင့် တရားဝင် allowed case နှစ်ခုလုံး ပြန်စမ်းပါ။

Control တစ်ခုစီအတွက် ကာကွယ်လိုသော asset နှင့် စစ်ဆေးရမည့် boundary ကို အမည်တပ်ပါ။ နမူနာ data ဖြင့် ခွင့်ရှိသောအခြေအနေနှင့် ခွင့်မရှိသောအခြေအနေ နှစ်မျိုးလုံး စမ်းပြီး တကယ့်ရလဒ်ကို မှတ်ပါ။ နမူနာတစ်ခု မှန်ကန်ခြင်းက ထို behavior ကိုသာ ထောက်ခံပြီး app တစ်ခုလုံး အားနည်းချက်မရှိကြောင်း လက်မှတ် မဟုတ်ပါ။
